arguments.command:
python -c "
import parse

# Test with named results
r = parse.parse('{name} is {age}', 'Alice is 30')
print('Named result:', r)
print('fixed:', r.fixed)
print('named:', r.named)
print()

# Test __contains__ with keys
print('\"name\" in r:', 'name' in r)
print('\"age\" in r:', 'age' in r)
print('\"nonexistent\" in r:', 'nonexistent' in r)
print()

# Test __contains__ with values
print('\"Alice\" in r:', 'Alice' in r)
print('\"30\" in r:', '30' in r)
print('99 in r:', 99 in r)
print()

# Test with fixed results only
r2 = parse.parse('{} {}', 'hello world')
print('Fixed result:', r2)
print('fixed:', r2.fixed)
print('named:', r2.named)
print()
print('\"hello\" in r2:', 'hello' in r2)
print('\"world\" in r2:', 'world' in r2)
print('\"foo\" in r2:', 'foo' in r2)
print()

# Test with mixed results
r3 = parse.parse('{a} and {}', 'one and two')
print('Mixed result:', r3)
print('fixed:', r3.fixed)
print('named:', r3.named)
print()
print('\"a\" in r3:', 'a' in r3)
print('\"one\" in r3:', 'one' in r3)
print('\"two\" in r3:', 'two' in r3)
"
